items.text:

questions.title: Comparing, Evaluating, and Replacing Algorithms for Matching Values in Sorted Arrays (Question 25, ITE 2015)

items.text: Consider the following two algorithms which perform the same function using two arrays. You can  assume that both arrays are indexed from 1 and that both arrays are sorted from smallest to largest.
What is the purpose of these algorithms?

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies the purpose of the algorithms.

markingRubricContentItem.text: To find the items which occur in both arrays (i.e. the intersection of the arrays).

items.text: MysteryAlgorithmTwo is substantially more efficient with larger input arrays than MysteryAlgorithmOne. Contrast the logic of these algorithms, particularly in terms of  how the efficiency benefit in MysteryAlgorithmTwo has been achieved.

criteria.criterion: Provides a comprehensive comparison of both algorithms and correctly explains how the  second algorithm is more efficient.
Provides a description of the logic of both algorithms.
Identifies an aspect of the logic in one of the algorithms.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
MysteryAlgorithmOne contains an outer loop and an inner loop. The outer loop iterates over every item  in arrayOne (we will say that this loop executes M times). Every time the outer loop executes, the inner  loop iterates over every value in arrayTwo (we will say this loop executes N times). Therefore, the  code within the inner loop (which checks whether the item occurs in both arrays) executes M * N  times. For an array with a large amount of data, this is a large number of comparisons and is very  inefficient. 

MysteryAlgorithmTwo takes a more efficient approach. It assumes that the arrays are sorted and  therefore can reduce the number of comparisons by iteratively reducing the lower bounds of the arrays  that need to be checked. This is done by eliminating the comparison of items when they are smaller  than the current item being evaluated. Only one loop is required, substantially improving efficiency.

items.text:
A routine based on the MysteryAlgorithmOne algorithm forms part of a larger  existing software package. The developers have decided to replace the inefficient MysteryAlgorithmOne based routine with the logic of the more efficient MysteryAlgorithmTwo. 

Explain how adopting a modular approach to designing the software system would  assist in this process. You should also reference features of the module itself which  have, or could be, implemented to improve reusability.

criteria.criterion: Explains the modular approach with reference to aspects of the modules which improve  reusability, along with additional recommendations for further improvement.
Explains the modular approach with reference to aspects of the modules which improve  reusability.
Identifies a feature of a modular approach to software design.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
A modular approach to designing the software system can assist in replacing the module, as the system  has been well-structured such that the various subroutines can be coded independently and are not  reliant on other parts of the system, apart from being called and provided with the relevant parameters.  In terms of the mystery algorithm modules, they have been coded to take parameters so they are self contained without the need to reference global variables. Both modules also have the same method  signature, so they are a direct replacement for each other – the rest of the system should be oblivious to  the fact that the content of the modules have been changed. 

One aspect which could be improved to assist reusability are the PRINT statements. This restricts the  usefulness of the module as it can only print the results to screen, rather than potentially using the  results for other processing in the system. The module should instead return a new array with the  relevant data. This is a much more versatile approach as the data could be printed or re-used in the  system.

questions.title: Outline why software developers use structure charts in the development of software. (Q29, ITE 2017)

items.text: Outline why software developers use structure charts in the development of software.

criteria.criterion: Shows an understanding of the role of structure charts in the development of software.
Identifies a feature of structure charts.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Structure charts show all the subroutines in a program and the relationships between them. They are useful because:

• during the development of the code, they provide a list of subroutines which need to be coded. As each is completed it can be ticked off and remaining subroutines can be seen at a glance.

• they show how subroutines interact with the subroutines around them. As a developer is writing the subroutine and during subsequent maintenance they can see which data is passed in, what data is returned, and what subroutines need to be called by the subroutine under development. Repetition and decision symbols give further insight into how subroutines should be called.

items.text:

• read from a file: employee names, hourly pay rate and number of hours worked in the last week

• calculate the pay for the employee

• calculate the tax for the employee

• print a payslip for each employee

Pre-existing subroutines are available which:

• calculate the weekly pay given the hourly pay rate and the number of hours worked

• determine the amount of tax which should be deducted given the weekly pay

• print a payslip given the employee name and the appropriate details

Draw a structure chart for the payroll software.

items.text:
A programmer wishes to use the following code fragments to swap the names of people in seats that are stored in an array.

 

BEGIN Seats

Input SeatNo1

Input SeatNo2

Swap(XXX, XXX)

END Seats

 

BEGIN Swap(a, b)

Temp = a

a = b

b = Temp

END Swap

The line Swap (XXX, XXX) is a call to a the sub module Swap.

Which of the following correctly replaces the  XXX, XXX ?

questions.title: Applying Quality Assurance and Testing Techniques to Improve Software Accuracy and Efficiency (Q23, CSSA 2019)

items.text: Explain how quality assurance can assist in the development of software.

criteria.criterion:
• Thoroughly explains how quality assurance processes assist in the development of software

  • Explicit criteria for ease of measurement

  • Ongoing process throughout development – helps documentation and implementation

  • Ensures user needs are met or exceeded
Explains how at least one aspect of quality assurance can assist in software development
Shows some understanding of quality assurance

items.text: Describe how the expected output of test data is useful in conducting meaningful tests of proposed solutions.

criteria.criterion: Describes why knowing expected results is important in the testing process
Shows some understanding of the testing process

items.text:
It is suggested by a colleague that a binary search should be used to find a particular element in the following array:

31

14

51

18

33

19

28

57

Describe strategies/techniques that could be implemented so that a successful search could be undertaken on this array.

criteria.criterion:
• Is able to show that the search could work if one of two things were done:

  • Using a sorting algorithm to sort the array and then apply the binary searching

  • Leaving the array as is but applying a linear search
Shows that one of the two that could make it work
